plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Trees cloaked in clouds of lavender-blue trumpet flowers that carpet streets and gardens with fallen purple blooms. In late spring the whole canopy glows, often before the leaves fully return.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southern Hemisphere cities such as Pretoria in South Africa, Sydney in Australia and Buenos Aires in Argentina
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, yet Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of trees lining its streets.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A graceful evergreen shrub whose silky, softly fragrant blossoms open just as most gardens are fading for winter. Petals drift down in drifts of pink and white beneath glossy dark leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Gardens of Japan, the southeastern United States and mild parts of western Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea, is a close relative of the sasanqua camellia.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense, many-petaled blooms in rich autumn shades that keep gardens and markets colorful when other flowers have faded. They flourish in the cool, short days of late fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, peaking from October to late November
plants.location: Gardens and flower markets across East Asia, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants: they set buds only when nights grow long, which is why they bloom so reliably in autumn.
